items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: And finally, after the evening was over, the five of us went to the cafeteria at Bickford's, I think it was. And it was Sidney and Bunk and Harold and my friend and myself.

ctx.x: He'd do things like that repeatedly, yeah. If I remember the other night you mentioned something, some detail escapes me now about Bechet and speaking about when he helped Louis and all that. That's right.

What was that? Well, there was a time when Bechet was playing at Ryan's and Harold Draub and a friend of mine from Baltimore and myself went into Ryan's to see Bechet and Bunk turned up and he had been drinking very heavily. And he was closer in the disorder that they often got in at such times. And he was sitting at our table and then he'd get up to the bandstand and be singing along with the tune. And he was having some kind of contest with Sidney about what... Trying to name tunes that Sidney couldn't…
Actually helped him with his horn.

items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-15
items.q: he was kind of hard to talk to for me, and, uh, hard to get to know.

ctx.x: Well, what about Bechet's personal auntie there? What would you know?

Well, Bechet seems to be a very quiet guy, very difficult to get to know. He, he, uh, I think he kind of shut people out. I mean, that's the way, that's the impression I got anyway. Uh, because he's a very sensitive guy and, and often disturbed, I guess, with personal problems or, or who knows what. But, I mean, uh, he was, wasn't unpleasant. He, he wasn't, uh, insulting. He, or he didn't offend, offend, uh, anyone by shutting them out. But yet, he, he was kind of hard to talk to for me, and, uh, hard to get to…
I guess Wilbur must have known him pretty well.
